result.question: Differentiate between demand-pull and cost-push inflation. Suggest measures to control each. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Propose practical measures and say who should act and how.

sentences.text: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, which erodes the purchasing power of money.
Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand exceeds the available supply of goods and services, often described as too much money chasing too few goods.
It is fuelled by rising incomes, easy credit or deficit financing.
Cost-push inflation arises when aggregate demand rises faster than output and pulls prices upwards.
Its usual triggers are higher wages, costlier raw materials and oil price shocks.
Demand-pull inflation is checked by tighter monetary policy, such as a higher repo rate, and by fiscal restraint through lower spending or higher taxes.
Cost-push inflation is eased by supply-side steps such as cutting excise and customs duties on inputs, importing goods in short supply and raising productivity.
Monetary tightening alone works poorly against price rises in items of daily use such as onions or wheat, because these are rarely bought on credit.
As Indian inflation often combines both, coordinated monetary, fiscal and supply-side action works best.
